[element-named-content]
=== `<named-content>` Named Special (Subject) Content

Word or phrase whose content/subject matter has distinct semantics or content-related significance that is not defined in this Tag Set.

#### Usage/Remarks
In print or display, such semantic content is likely to be treated differently, for example, given a stand-out typographic style such as italics or background shading.

#### Related Elements

*Named/Styled Content Best Practice:* The related <<element-styled-content,`<styled-content>`>> element may, in some instances, produce the same look on print or display as some `<named-content>` elements. Both mark content that has a visual distinction; the difference between the two elements is intent. If it is known that this word is in italics because it is a genus or species name, this semantics should be preserved with a `<named-content>` element with a <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>> attribute of “genus-species” or equivalent. The <<element-styled-content,`<styled-content>`>> element would merely tell you that it was always in green shaded background `style="green-shading"` or in italics.
*Specific Use:* Being web-only or print-only is not a stylistic matter, but rather a particular _use_, which should be tagged with the <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>> attribute on the appropriate element, perhaps even on a `<named-content>` or <<element-styled-content,`<styled-content>`>> element.

#### Tagged Sample

##### Temperature and duration semantics
[source,xml]
....
...
<p>As a minimum, testing is required at nominal ambient and highest ambient 
values, typically <named-content content-type="temp">70 °C</named-content> 
and <named-content content-type="temp">85 °C</named-content> for at least 
<named-content content-type="duration">one hour</named-content>.</p>
...
....
